issues.legal_issue: Trustees may not abdicate their office by transferring all trust functions and trust property to a replacement body unless the trust instrument authorizes it or the beneficiaries consent.
material_facts: The trust deed appointed trustees to manage the school and its properties, permitted them to appoint new trustees and to make rules for the school's efficient operation, but did not authorize replacement of the trustees as a body.

The trustees handed management of the school to a society and transferred the properties to its governing body, thereby transferring all their functions and powers rather than delegating particular tasks.
The trust deed did not authorize this substitution, and there was no consent by the beneficiary or permission of the court.
issues.conclusion: The transfer was an unlawful abdication; the society and its governing-body members did not become trustees of the trust properties.
issues.legal_principle: A trustee who has accepted a trust cannot renounce it except with court permission, beneficiary consent, or authority in the trust instrument, and cannot delegate the office or its functions except in specified circumstances. Sections 46 and 47 of the Indian Trusts Act embody these principles, although section 1 makes the Act inapplicable in terms to public or private religious or charitable endowments. The principles nevertheless apply to trusts generally. A power to appoint new trustees permits the existing trustees to add to their number, not to replace themselves; a power to frame rules does not authorize them to surrender management or transfer trust property. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: trust_administration_case and trustees_transferred_all_functions and not deed_authorized_substitution and not beneficiaries_consented and not court_permitted_renunciation

predicates.trust_administration_case: The proceeding concerns the administration of property held on trust.
predicates.trustees_transferred_all_functions: The appointed trustees transferred the whole management and all trust functions to another body rather than delegating particular tasks.
predicates.deed_authorized_substitution: The trust instrument authorized the appointed trustees to replace themselves with another body.
predicates.beneficiaries_consented: The beneficiaries consented to the trustees' surrender of their duties and functions.
predicates.court_permitted_renunciation: A court permitted the trustees to renounce their trust.

issues.definition: If appointed trustees transfer all their functions in a trust-administration case without authority in the trust instrument, beneficiary consent, or court permission, the replacement body does not become trustee.

issues.legal_issue: A decree granting relief against defendants is improper when the plaint, read as a whole, neither seeks relief against them nor alleges a basis for that relief.
material_facts: The proceeding was a suit concerning the administration of trust property.
Some defendants were named in the suit, but the plaint's allegations and its requested relief concerned the society and its governing-body members, not those defendants.
The lower courts granted relief against the defendants against whom no relief had been sought, and those defendants appealed.
issues.conclusion: The decree against the defendants against whom no relief had been sought was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The relief sought must be determined by reading the plaint as a whole; general references to “defendants” do not amount to a claim for relief against every named defendant where the allegations and context identify only some of them. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this holding.

predicates.appeal_from_decree: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decree that granted relief against defendants.
predicates.plaint_read_as_whole_identifies_other_de: The plaint, considered as a whole, identifies defendants other than the target defendants as the persons against whom relief is sought.
predicates.no_allegations_support_relief_against_ta: The plaint contains no allegations supporting relief against the target defendants.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges relief granted against defendants whom the plaint does not identify as targets of relief and against whom it alleges no supporting grounds, that decree is improper.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot avoid the consequences of its pleaded position that disputed properties are trust properties by advancing an inconsistent contention for the first time on appeal.
material_facts: The defendants' written statement accepted that the properties listed in the plaint were covered by the trust and claimed that they had become trustees of those properties under the trust deed.
The defendants maintained that position before the trial court and the High Court.
On appeal, they argued that the trust deed covered only specified properties belonging to its settlors and not the other listed properties.
issues.conclusion: The court rejected the new contention and treated the properties listed in the plaint as covered by the trust for purposes of the dispute.
issues.legal_principle: The court relied on the defendants' unequivocal written pleading and their consistent case in the lower courts, which accepted that the listed properties were covered by the trust. It did not accept the inconsistent contention newly advanced on appeal. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this holding.

predicates.appeal_in_trust_property_dispute: The proceeding is an appeal in a dispute about whether identified properties are held on trust.
predicates.prior_pleading_admitted_property_coverag: A party's earlier pleading accepted that the disputed properties were covered by the trust.
predicates.prior_case_claimed_trusteeship_over_thos: The party maintained in the lower courts that it held the properties as trustee under the trust instrument.
predicates.appellate_argument_contradicts_prior_pos: On appeal, the party advanced a claim about the properties that contradicted its earlier pleaded and maintained position.

issues.definition: When a party admitted trust coverage and claimed trusteeship over the properties in the lower courts, a contradictory property-coverage argument advanced on appeal is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: Persons who lack valid appointment as trustees but possess and manage trust property are liable to removal from its management and to account for their administration.
material_facts: A body had taken possession of and managed the trust properties after the appointed trustees unlawfully transferred the management and properties to it.
The body and its members had not been validly appointed trustees under the trust deed.
The plaintiffs sought their removal from management and an account of their administration.
issues.conclusion: The body and its members were to be removed from management and were liable to account for their entire period of management.
issues.legal_principle: Because the purported trustees had no legal right to remain in possession of the trust properties, they could be removed from management; their management as trustees de son tort made them liable to account for the entire period. The court did not need to decide the separate allegations of misapplication or the admission of students outside the community. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this holding.

predicates.public_trust_management_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking relief concerning the management of public trust property.
predicates.body_managed_trust_property: A body possessed and administered property held on trust.
predicates.body_was_not_validly_appointed_trustee: The body did not acquire valid appointment as trustee under the trust instrument or another lawful basis.

issues.definition: In a suit over public trust management, a body that administered trust property without valid appointment is removable from management and must account for its administration.

issues.legal_issue: Where the existing trustees cannot effectively administer the trust and a scheme is unnecessary, new trustees may be appointed without framing a scheme.
material_facts: Nearly all of the originally appointed trustees had died; the sole surviving trustee was too old to administer the trust successfully and had not performed trustee functions for many years.
The plaintiffs accepted that a scheme for administration was not necessary, at least at that time.
The court directed the trial court to appoint suitable new trustees after allowing the plaintiffs and other responsible community members to make recommendations and objections.
issues.conclusion: A scheme was not necessary at that time, but suitable new trustees were to be appointed by the trial court.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered a scheme unnecessary at least for the present, while the death or incapacity and prolonged inactivity of the existing trustees made appointment of new trustees necessary. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this remedial direction.

predicates.trust_administration_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the administration of a trust.
predicates.existing_trustees_cannot_effectively_adm: The existing trustees are deceased, unable, or have been inactive so that they cannot effectively administer the trust.
predicates.scheme_is_unnecessary: The court considers a formal scheme unnecessary for the trust's administration.

issues.definition: When existing trustees cannot effectively administer a trust and a formal scheme is unnecessary, new trustees should be appointed without framing a scheme.
